models.architecture_or_algorithm: Convolutional and recurrent neural network layers
models.dataset_source_or_link: provided through the web server (not specified in evidence)
models.candidate_reason: Deep learning model for AMP recognition, openly available web server, benchmarked against state-of-the-art
models.evidence: We propose a neural network model with convolutional and recurrent layers that leverage primary sequence composition. Models and datasets are made freely available through the Antimicrobial Peptide Scanner vr.2 web server at www.ampscanner.com. The server uses a deep neural network (DNN) as a prediction tool, considering a peptide with prediction probability > 0.5 as an AMP. (Additional evidence from PMID 37851665 and PMID 39203524)

models.candidate_reason: Deep learning (LSTM) model for AMP classification, potentially useful for benchmark
models.evidence: A bidirectional LSTM classification model was constructed to design short novel AMP sequences with potential antibacterial activity against E. coli. ... validation accuracies of the classification models were 81.6-88.9% and the novel AMPs were classified as antimicrobial with accuracies of 70.6-91.7%.

important_evidence: AMPScanner v2 uses convolutional and recurrent neural network layers, primary sequence composition, and provides a web server at www.ampscanner.com.
LSTM-based classifier (Wang et al. 2021) achieved validation accuracies of 81.6-88.9% and novel AMP classification accuracies of 70.6-91.7%.
PepGen 1.0 is an LSTM-based AMP generator accessible via a shortened URL, used to generate 3006 sequences.
AmPepGen is a GAN-based AMP generator with code available at https://github.com/Anorpe/ampepgen-dev.
AMPScanner v2 was utilized in benchmark studies (PMID 37851665, PMID 39203524) for AMP prediction.
uncertainties: Exact composition and size of the AMPScanner training dataset unknown from available evidence.
No code repository or web server for the LSTM-based classifier (Wang et al. 2021).
DOI mismatch for the Wang et al. paper: 10.1016/j.diagmicrobio.2004.02.008 does not correspond to the 2021 paper; possible indexing error.
PepGen 1.0 web server is provided as a shortened URL, stability and accessibility uncertain.
Relevance of tAMPer (peptide toxicity prediction model, PMID 39196703) to antimicrobial peptide prediction is unclear.
